 As his re-election victory became apparent Tuesday night, Senator Chris Coons celebrated with fellow Democrats in Wilmington, exclaiming "there is change in the air."
 Senator Chris Coons, Auditor of Accounts Lydia York, Treasurer-elect Ted Lauzen, Attorney General Kathy Jennings celebrate at Democratic Party headquarters Tuesday
 photo: WDEL's Mark Fowser 
 Coons, in office for 16 years, will start another six-year term in January. The change to which he is referring is a Democratic-led House and Senate during the final two years of the administration of President Trump.
 "There is a new future in front of us. There is hope right before us," Coons continued. 
 Coons said he hopes to introduce a bill that would have a middle class tax cut for day care, education, housing and in-home healthcare, and "deal with the costs that are making people's lives miserable and bring 'joy in the morning.'"
 Runner-up, Republican Dr. Mike Katz, said he felt his campaign carried a good message. "We fought to lower living costs, fix healthcare, protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, and ensure that veterans receive their earned care and benefits. We called for term limits, responsible balanced budgets, and independent leadership accountable to the people."
 Katz congratulated Coons on his victory, adding "now, I challenge you to lead beyond the divisions of political parties and serve all Delawareans, move beyond the constant messaging about fighting President Trump, work with him where you can advance Delaware's interests... where you disagree, offer constructive alternative."
